rationale.conceptual: The target is obtained by a textbook DFT operation: set up a known crystal structure, choose pseudopotentials, run a spin-polarized SCF calculation, and extract projected moments. No custom method of the paper must be implemented. It is essentially an off-the-shelf use of a standard library/code.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of a single load-bearing step (run DFT and extract moments) preceded by a trivial structure preparation. There is no multi-stage orchestration, no fragile tooling, and no complex data acquisition. It is a single script producing one artifact.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running a standard spin-polarized DFT calculation to reproduce site-projected magnetic moments. The method is a routine application of an established code (e.g., Quantum Espresso), not a novel algorithm. Execution is a single well-defined step with trivial preparation, producing one CSV file. Resources: a CPU-only DFT calculation on a ~66-atom cell, moderate memory and no GPU.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The paper's DFT calculation uses a moderately sized unit cell (hexagonal cell with 66 atoms). A modern plane-wave CPU-only DFT code would require a few GB of RAM and several core-hours, but no GPU. Input data (crystal structure) is negligible in size.
